root_cause.text: The error path in mshv_map_user_memory() directly calls vfree() to free the region without unregistering the associated MMU notifier, leaving the notifier active and pointing to freed memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `vfree(region)` with `mshv_region_put(region)` in the error path. The commit message explicitly states that "calling vfree() directly on the region leaves the MMU notifier registered" and that "when userspace later unmaps the memory, the notifier fires and accesses the freed region, causing a use-after-free." The fix uses mshv_region_put() which properly unregisters the MMU notifier before freeing the region, preventing the notifier from accessing freed memory after userspace unmaps the memory.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable function mshv_map_user_memory() is present in this commit. In the error path starting at line 1668 (errout label), when mshv_partition_mem_region_map(region) fails, the code directly calls vfree(region) without unregistering any associated MMU notifier. The function mshv_partition_create_region() allocates the region via vzalloc() at line 1618, and if the subsequent mapping operations fail, the error handling at line 1668 simply frees the region with vfree(region) without proper cleanup of MMU notifiers that may have been registered. This leaves any active MMU notifier pointing to the freed memory, which is the root cause of the vulnerability described.
